summary: S&P 500 closed at 7,543.64 on Jul 9 (+0.81%), about 0.9% below the Jun 2 all-time high of 7,609.78 — Nasdaq +1.3%, Dow +139pts, led by chip names (Micron +5.2%, Sandisk +7.6%, Applied Materials +3.2%) on renewed AI-demand optimism. VIX spiked above 18 intraday Thursday on a fresh Middle East tension flare-up before fading back below 17 by the close (16.90) — the market shrugged the geopolitical scare off within the same session rather than carrying fear into Friday. Breadth is strong at roughly 70% of S&P 500 names above their 50-day moving average, and the index sits comfortably above both its 50-day (~7,403) and 200-day (~6,948) averages — a genuinely healthy technical picture. New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh held his first FOMC meeting at 3.50–3.75% with a hawkish tilt to the median 2026 dot (implying a possible hike, not a cut), and Governor Waller's Jul 6 Rome speech called for more data-flexible forward guidance rather than pre-committing — both readable as 'no imminent move, but don't get complacent on cuts.' The near-term calendar is light until Jun CPI on Jul 14, then a real event cluster forms: GOOGL earnings Jul 22, then FOMC (Jul 28–29) colliding with MSFT/META/AAPL/AMZN earnings and Jun PCE in the same week. New cash: small selective entries are reasonable now through Jul 13, then pause into the CPI print and reassess.
